title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
Back to Blog
May 19, 2025
The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
e-commerce
Digital Payments
Luciano Decourt Ferrari
Chief Sales Officer at Getnet Brazil
The ability to shop online has fast become a baseline expectation for consumers when making purchases. Since gaining mainstream popularity over 20 years ago, eCommerce has continued to experience relentless growth. In fact, global eCommerce sales are expected to total $4.8 trillion this year and represent 23% of all retail sales by 2027.
This digital revolution transcends borders, with online retail sales in Latin America expected to increase from 12.3% of total retail sales in 2023 to 15.9% by 2028. In Europe, Spain’s eCommerce sector is estimated to generate $51 billion in revenue in 2025.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
There are various factors that will play a significant role in influencing eCommerce’s future trajectory. Namely, changing consumer expectations. How businesses adapt to keep up with these shifting demands – for example, by adopting the latest payment technologies – will determine how successful their eCommerce strategies are in coming years. This article will discuss the key needs of today’s online shoppers and steps businesses can take to ensure they’re meeting them.
Speed, convenience and zero friction

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text: The popularity of eCommerce has largely been driven by consumers love for convenience. Originally, online desktop shopping enabled people to make purchases from the comfort of their own homes. Now, mobile commerce means shopping can also be done on the go, no matter where people are. In Portugal 36% of total eCommerce sales are made via mobile. In neighbouring Spain, even higher levels of mobile adoption are present, with 66% of consumers regularly making purchases via smartphones. Latin America demonstrates a similar uptake of mobile shopping, with 59% of online retail sales made on mobile devices.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text: Whether waiting for a train, taking a lunch break, or lounging at home, mobile commerce means consumers can make purchases within seconds. To enable these anytime, anywhere shopping experiences, businesses should look to add mobile payment solutions to their offering - for example Digital Wallets, such as Apple Pay or Google Pay, QR Code payments; and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) apps such as Klarna and Afterpay.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text: Today’s consumers also demand payment processes so seamless they’re virtually invisible. Because of this, real-time payments are becoming increasingly popular for online shopping, with Spain leading adoption in Europe at 53% of all transactions (95% of which are made via Bizum). Further, acceleration is evident in Portugal, where MB Way users surged from 520,000 to over five million in just six years, and across Latin America, where Brazil's Pix system facilitated transactions totalling over 27 trillion reais in 2024. In eCommerce especially, Pix’s growth is remarkable: 70% of online merchants in the country are now accepting Pix, withan expectation that the solution will account for 38% of online sales by 2026.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
These developments are more than just an expectation for convenience; they’re becoming an essential competitive advantage. Businesses that integrate frictionless, real-time payment technologies will capture greater market share looking to the future.
Trust in transactions
Security is a key consideration for most consumers when making payments online, heightened by data breaches becoming more common across global markets. For instance, this January, Spain’s national Data Protection Authority – Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) – issued the highest number of GDPR fines in the EU, including fines for breaches affecting millions of customers. Further, Latin American companies suffer 40% more cyber-attacks per week than the global average.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text: To maintain consumer trust in eCommerce, businesses must implement robust security measures. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are two technologies that are integral to enhancing the security of payments, with sophisticated fraud detection systems able to identify and prevent fraudulent transactions as they happen. These AI applications are strengthened by tokenisation, which replaces sensitive payment data with unique identification symbols that retain essential information without compromising security. This creates an additional layer of protection that renders intercepted data useless to criminals.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text: AI-powered fraud detection uses real-time anomaly recognition and behavioural biometrics to identify suspicious patterns instantly, while sophisticated authentication mechanisms combine multi-factor verification with adaptive risk assessment to validate user identities contextually. Further, biometric authentication methods, like fingerprint and facial recognition, process sensitive data within secure device enclaves to create a frictionless and secure payment experience.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
Businesses can also maintain security transparency by offering reassurances through certifications or partnerships with trusted cybersecurity firms. These interlocking technologies and practices create a resilient security ecosystem that protects sensitive data, while maintaining operational efficiency and enhancing customer trust.
The personalisation-privacy paradox
Innovative Today’s shoppers also expect their online shopping experience to be fashioned specifically for them. In fact, 56% of Spanish consumers prefer brands that offer tailored experiences. This shift is being reflected by the implementation of AI technologies that can create personalised experiences – such as product recommendations based on browsing and purchase history.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
To meet these needs, this year, over 55% of total investments in the Portuguese IT sector are expected to flow toward digital transformation initiatives, with AI playing a central role. This signals an understanding among retailers that meeting rising consumer expectations requires technological advancement. Pivoting towards AI enabled solutions will enable retailers to deliver the tailored experiences that today’s consumer view as standard service.
However, alongside the demand for personalisation, there's growing concern about data privacy. This creates a "privacy paradox" where consumers want personalised experiences but remain worried about how their data is used. Latin Americans are particularly cautious about sharing personal information online, with 41% limiting what they share.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
For eCommerce merchants, being transparent about data collection practices is crucial. To truly gain consumer’s loyalty, it’s important to gain their trust. Merchants can earn that through clear communication about how their customer’s data is being used to personalise experiences.
Latin Americans are particularly cautious about sharing personal information online, with 41% limiting what they share.
AI-powered customer support
AI is also helping businesses transform customer service, which consumers are increasingly demanding to be immediate and personalised. The evolution of AI assistants reflects the growing desire for seamless service experiences - from simple chatbots to complex support systems capable of managing entire customer journeys.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text: These advanced, AI-powered customer service systems work by leveraging several sophisticated technologies to deliver personalised experiences. Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithms analyse customer text and speech by extracting intent, entities and sentiment. Deep learning models trained on millions of conversations recognise patterns in customer inquiries, while emotional intelligence capabilities detect subtle tonal shifts, frustration signals and satisfaction indicators by analysing language and voice patterns. These systems then employ real-time sentiment analysis to evaluate customer emotions and generate appropriate responses. Systems access customer history, preferences, and behaviour patterns to create completely tailored interactions.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text: With over eight in ten Spanish consumers stating that they would engage with support chatbots powered by AI and 56% of Latin American companies reporting positive impacts after using AI chatbots, the merchants that successfully implement these support systems will gain a significant competitive advantage. This will result in enhanced loyalty, increased lifetime value and more efficient operations.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
Beyond direct customer interactions, AI is revolutionising other touchpoints in the consumer journey. For example, AI-powered dynamic pricing algorithms can analyse market conditions, competitors' prices and customer behaviours to optimise price points that maximise sales and profits. Further, AI-powered recommendation engines can analyse purchase history, browsing behaviour and similar customer profiles to suggest tailored products at checkout. For merchants this increases the average spend per basket and for consumers it enhances the shopping experience.
Sustainability concerns

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
Finally, sustainability has become another critical factor determining the success of eCommerce businesses. In Portugal, traffic to sustainability-focused pages on major ecommerce platforms surged by 187% over the past year. Yet scepticism is growing, with 42% of environmental claims by Spanish companies deemed questionable and 58% of "eco-friendly" products lacking proper verification.
To address consumers ongoing concerns, businesses need to be transparent and verify their sustainability claims. Merchants wanting to get ahead in this area should also adopt eco-friendly packaging and educate consumers on environmental topics, to demonstrate their ongoing sustainability commitment.

title: The future of eCommerce: How modern shoppers are changing the way they pay
text:
For eCommerce businesses targeting Spanish, Portuguese and Latin American markets, success will depend on meeting the evolving consumer expectations in these regions. Those who navigate these ever-changing demands by integrating the right innovative technology will be best positioned to thrive in the future.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
Back to Blog
February 11, 2025
The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
Payment Trends
Spain & Portugal
Ruben Justel
CEO of Getnet Europe
The payment landscape across Spain and Portugal is set to undergo a transformation in 2025, driven by technological innovations and a relentless focus on customer experience. These changes will redefine how consumers and businesses interact with payment technology.
The year of ‘invisible’ payments
In 2025, the payment industry needs to accelerate to meet consumers’ ever-growing demands for faster, simpler and more intuitive payment experiences. Today’s consumers expect the payment process to be so seamless it’s virtually invisible – an effortless part of their daily transactions.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
One payment method leading the charge when it comes to speed and simplicity is real time payments. With instant credit transfers, the money is available in the payee’s account in just a few seconds, 24/7, 365 days a year.
Spain has emerged as a European leader in real-time payments adoption, with this method accounting for 53% of all transactions – significantly higher than the European average of 15%. Its popularity is in part thanks to the collaborative initiative by the Spanish financial sector to create Bizum, a mobile payment service that allows users to send and receive money, designed to meet digital-first consumers’ demands. And there are no signs of slowing down, with real-time payments projected to achieve a 16.8% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) by 2030.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
Similarly, Portugal has experienced growth in the adoption of real-time payments over the past couple of years. MB Way, a mobile payment system that allows users to make purchases, transfer money and withdraw cash using their phone, grew from 520,000 users in 2017 to over five million users in September 2023. It’s quickly becoming the Portuguese’s favourite mobile payment method.
The adoption rates of real-time payments in Spain and Portugal illustrate that the message is clear; consumers want real-time payments. Ultimately, success will depend on merchants’ having the right technology to meet the needs of consumers without compromising on customer experience.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
The rise of social commerce:
A large majority of Gen Z grew up online and therefore, social media plays a huge role in their lives. With 74.5% of Gen Zers spending their free time online, what they see on social media platforms is going to influence their lives including their purchasing decisions.
Social commerce – the purchases of goods and services directly within social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok – is on the rise, and king among Gen Z shoppers. With an estimated 5 billion social media users worldwide in 2023, the social commerce market is growing faster than traditional e-commerce and shows no signs of slowing down. Forecasts predict that social commerce sales will reach $2.9 trillion by 2026.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
Bridging the digital-physical divide
Another area with high consumer expectations in 2025 is the seamless bridge between physical and digital shopping experiences. Shoppers now expect to be able to move effortlessly between online browsing and in-store visits, with their preferences, payment methods, and loyalty rewards automatically syncing across all channels. The traditional divide between eCommerce and physical retail has dissolved, replaced by a fluid commerce ecosystem where starting a purchase on a mobile device and completing it in-store, or vice versa, feels natural.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
In Spain, this transformation is evident through the growing prevalence of Research Online, Purchase Offline (ROPO). Nearly 75% of Spanish consumers prefer to research products digitally before making the trip to buy in-store and 76% combine purchases both online and in-store.
Meanwhile, in Portugal, while consumers are also embracing a hybrid approach to shopping, their preference remains with brick-and-mortar stores. 97% of consumers shopped in-store in 2024, compared to 22% who shopped online. However, eCommerce has been growing rapidly in the region, with experts predicting the market size to reach $9.98 billion by 2029, almost double what was predicted for 2024. Portuguese consumers also enjoy shopping on their phones, with mobile commerce accounting for 36% of e-commerce.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
Ultimately, merchants need to invest in good omnichannel experiences so consumers can seamlessly move from shopping online to in-store and vice versa.
Nearly 75% of Spanish consumers prefer to research products digitally before making the trip to buy in-store and 76% combine purchases both online and in-store.
AI-watchdog – the future of security
As merchants strive to enhance customer experiences across multiple channels, they must simultaneously strengthen their digital infrastructure with advanced security measures. Artificial Intelligence (AI) takes centre stage in security and fraud prevention across the world. With security the foundation of consumer trust, investment in AI-powered fraud prevention tools needs to be top of mind for merchants.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text: Spain is emerging as a notable pioneer in AI-driven fraud prevention. The country launched Europe's first AI regulatory agency which signals a commitment to developing an inclusive and citizen-centred framework for AI implementation. Their position as a pioneer is exemplified by Iberpay, who manage the Spanish payment system by connecting banks, companies and citizens to process and settle their payments, integrating AI and machine learning into their Payguard anti-fraud service. Payguard was developed by Iberpay and is a collection of five tools that work together to help identify, prevent and anticipate fraud.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text: Although Portugal isn’t quite matching Spain’s pace when it comes to AI adoption, the country is making significant strides in its AI capabilities. As a member of the EU, Portugal has implemented regulatory compliance and ICT risk management frameworks under the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). This aligns with the EU-wide effort to enhance digital resilience in the financial sector and protect against cyber threats. The ‘AI Portugal 2030’ strategy supports AI research, workforce retraining and economic growth through AI technologies, signalling a desire to push forward the country’s adoption of this technology.

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
Europe as whole is moving towards more advanced, AI-driven solutions to combat financial crime and improve regulatory compliance. For merchants in Spain and Portugal it’s important to stay ahead of the curve and invest in AI-powered security, customer support and fraud prevention. Security remains the fundamental cornerstone for trust so AI will help merchants increase customer loyalty.
Looking ahead

title: The 2025 payments landscape in Spain and Portugal
text:
In 2025 merchants will be defined by their commitment to offering instant payments, creating good omnichannel experiences and investing in AI-powered security methods. Merchants in Spain and Portugal that successfully bridge the digital-physical divide while maintaining robust security will thrive in this new landscape, where speed and simplicity coexist with safety and trust. The Iberian Peninsula’s payments landscape is set to experience great change, and merchants who are ready to capitalise on this will experience strong growth this year.

text:
June 21, 2025
Meliá Hotels International and Getnet are pioneers in payment security in Latin America, offering P2PE solutions.
Mexico
Travel
Meliá Hotels International, one of the world's leading hotel chains, was faced with a significant challenge in relation to its operations in Latin America: the implementation of a card-present payment solution certified under the most rigorous security standard on the market, Point-to-Point Encryption (P2PE).
This requirement was driven by both its own stringent internal security policies and the need to simplify compliance with the PCI DSS standard.

title: Meliá Hotels International and Getnet are pioneers in payment security in Latin America, offering P2PE solutions.
text:
In response to this need, Getnet led the development of the first certified P2PE solution in the region through its Technology Hub in Mexico (MIT), marking a milestone in the Latin American payments industry.
P2PE: total protection from the point of interaction.
P2PE (Point-to-Point Encryption) solution encrypts sensitive card data at the point of sale and keeps it encrypted throughout the payment journey until processing. This protects cardholder data in transit, significantly reducing the risk of data exfiltration and ensuring that information cannot be intercepted, stolen or manipulated.
Implementing a P2PE-certified solution offers merchants significant benefits:

title: Meliá Hotels International and Getnet are pioneers in payment security in Latin America, offering P2PE solutions.
text:
Reduced PCI DSS compliance scope and costs, minimising audits and validation efforts.
Peace of mind that comes with having a solution validated to the highest security standards.
An improved payment experience for customers, including:
Faster and more efficient transactions
Increased security of personal data adn card-presen
Protection against fraud and identity theft
Increased trust in the merchant
"From its inception, we identified the benefits of the project for the market and felt it was necessary to develop it, given the high technical capabilities required”
Alberto González, CISO - MIT ( a Getnet company)
A technological challenge and a pioneering solution

title: Meliá Hotels International and Getnet are pioneers in payment security in Latin America, offering P2PE solutions.
text:
When Meliá first expressed its need, there was no certified P2PE solution available in Latin America. This was a significant challenge, but also an opportunity for innovation.
Getnet's Technology Hub in Mexico (MIT) accepted the challenge, launching a project led by its cybersecurity team, with high technical requirements in terms of cryptography and risk management.
In addition to developing the P2PE solution from scratch, the project faced another challenge in the form of integration with Opera Cloud, Meliá's recently adopted hotel management system.

title: Meliá Hotels International and Getnet are pioneers in payment security in Latin America, offering P2PE solutions.
text:
The P2PE standard requires compliance with over 500 security requirements organised around three pillars: people, processes, and technology. To meet these requirements, MIT adapted its internal processes and developed its technology, ensuring a robust, flexible and scalable solution.
The result matched the Meliá brand
The outcome was a card-present payment solution:
P2PE certified.
Fully integrated with Opera Cloud
Thanks to this development, Meliá is able to comply with its internal security policies and optimise its regulatory compliance, while also enhancing its customers' experience by ensuring fully secure electronic payments.

title: Meliá Hotels International and Getnet are pioneers in payment security in Latin America, offering P2PE solutions.
text:
"Getnet is a very important partner for Meliá. They provide us with the crucial technology needed to meet our customers' needs at the moment of purchase. This project is extremely valuable to our company, and we plan to implement it worldwide”
Gaspar Llabrés, Head of the Credit and Insurance Department at Meliá
A scalable solution for the hotel, retail and restaurant sectors
The successful implementation of the P2PE solution, developed by MIT and deployed by Getnet at Meliá, demonstrates its applicability not only to the hotel sector, but also to other industries. For instance, the retail and restaurant sectors, where secure face-to-face payments are essential.

title: Getnet is promoting the arrival of Bizum at physical point-of-sale (POS) terminals
text:
October 16, 2025
Getnet is promoting the arrival of Bizum at physical point-of-sale (POS) terminals
Spain
This transition from digital commerce to physical stores is a significant step in establishing Bizum as a omnichannel payment method in Spain.
In recent years, the payments sector has undergone profound transformation. Consumers and businesses no longer want to wait a day or two for transfers to clear. Digitisation has raised expectations, making immediacy the norm.
Instant payments are the answer to this demand, enabling money transfers to be processed in under 10 seconds, and available 24/7, 365 days a year. This shift is reshaping the payment ecosystem, making speed and availability as important as security and trust.

title: Getnet is promoting the arrival of Bizum at physical point-of-sale (POS) terminals
text:
The adoption of instant payments is evident worldwide, with different regions advancing at different speeds.
In 2024 alone, Brazil's PIX, a real-time instant payment system launched by the country's central bank, processed 64 billion transactions. By the end of 2027, PIX is projected to surpass credit cards in Brazil, capturing 51% of the market.
Mexico processed 5.3 billion real-time payments through its SPEI infrastructure in 2024.
Spain has become one of the European leaders in the adoption of instant payments, which represented 56% of all transfers made in the country in 2024.
Bizum: a catalyst for instant payments in Spain

title: Getnet is promoting the arrival of Bizum at physical point-of-sale (POS) terminals
text:
Launched in 2016, Bizum was a joint initiative by Spanish banks in response to the demand for real-time money transfers between individuals. The concept was simple yet powerful: users could send and receive money using only a mobile number, eliminating the need for an IBAN or any other bank details.
In just a few years, Bizum has evolved from emerging technology to social standard. It has influenced everyday language – 'Send me a Bizum' is a phrase that didn’t exist just a few years ago, but is now widely used. We can now send money, split expenses, make donations and shop online in seconds, without even thinking about it.
Bizum's success lies in the user experience:

title: Getnet is promoting the arrival of Bizum at physical point-of-sale (POS) terminals
text:
Simplicity: just select a contact from your address book and send the money.
Speed: the recipient receives the funds in seconds.
Availability: just select it works 24 hours a day, including weekends and bank holidays.
Bizum's growth has been spectacular. In the first nine months of this year, it reached 30 million active users and processed 900 million transactions. These figures confirm that Bizum is not only the most successful instant payment system in Spain, but also one of the most widespread in Europe. More than 90% of Spanish accounts are able to send and receive instant transfers.
From mobile to in-store: Getnet is partnering with Bizum to take the next step.

title: Getnet is promoting the arrival of Bizum at physical point-of-sale (POS) terminals
text:
Although Bizum was initially developed as a person-to-person (P2P) payment method, it has evolved into a much broader ecosystem:
eCommerce: today, thousands of online stores allow customers to pay using their mobile number and Bizum password, offering a fast and secure process.
Payments to the government: the Tax Agency and public bodies already accept Bizum for certain procedures and fee payments.
Physical commerce: Bizum is now being trialled at POS terminals, paving the way for mobile payments in physical shops without the need for a digital card.

title: Getnet is promoting the arrival of Bizum at physical point-of-sale (POS) terminals
text:
Getnet is currently testing Bizum payments at its own POS terminals with the aim of providing the same experience for in-store payments as online. This functionality is expected to be fully operational by the end of the year, enabling any business with a Getnet card reader to accept Bizum payments in the same way as card or contactless methods.
For merchants, this means diversifying payment methods, facilitating sales to customers who don’t want to use cards, and improving cash flow by accessing funds instantly.
For consumers, Bizum offers a simpler alternative, as payments can be made using only a mobile number, so there is no need to carry a digital card.

text:
Arthur Bedel, fintech and payment influencer and Connecting the Dots partner, experienced Bizum payments at Madrid Santander Work Café using Getnet's Get Smart POS terminal.
This transition from digital commerce to physical stores is a significant step in establishing Bizum as a omnichannel payment method in Spain, and Getnet is playing a pivotal role in this process.

Prima simultaneamente a tecla amarela e o botão "#". Quando o ecrã se ligar, prima a tecla verde (OK).

Pode contactar a linha de apoio Getnet através do número 800 274 274, marcar a opção 1 > 3 e os nossos técnicos ajudarão a resolver o problema.

Para ligar o seu TPA, primeiro ligue o terminal à sua bateria e prima a tecla verde durante alguns segundos.

Verifone: Seleccione o menu "Supervisor" e prima "Activar TPA".
Petrotec: Premir a tecla "menu/func" e seleccionar a opção "supervisor". Em seguida, premir "activar (abrir)".

title: TPA fora de serviço: como reativar o equipamento?
text: Nova nota, modelo Spg7: Com cartão de supervisor: Se a mensagem "Out of service" aparecer no visor da TPA, premir a tecla 00 com a seta para baixo para "Supervisor" e confirmar com a tecla verde "Ok". Premir novamente a tecla 00 com a seta para baixo para "Ativar TPA" e premir "Ok". Aparecerá a mensagem "Supervisor card", seleccionar "Use". Terá então de segurar o cartão, introduzir o código secreto e validar com "Ok". Será emitido um recibo de activação e a mensagem "Em serviço" aparecerá no ecrã. Sem cartão de supervisor: Se o ecrã TPA exibir a mensagem "Out of service", prima a tecla 00 com a seta para baixo até chegar a "Supervisor" e confirme com a tecla verde "Ok". Prima, novamente, a tecla 00 com a seta para baixo até "Activar TPA" e confirme com "Ok".

title: TPA fora de serviço: como reativar o equipamento?
text: Outros modelos: Com cartão de supervisor: se o visor do TPA mostrar a mensagem "Out of service", prima a tecla de seta para baixo para "Supervisor" e confirme com a tecla verde "Ok". Depois, premir a tecla de seta para cima para "Activate" e premir "Ok". Premir novamente a tecla de seta para cima e seleccionar " 1 - Utilizar". Terá então de manter o cartão premido, introduzir o código secreto e confirmar com "Ok". Será emitido um recibo de activação e a mensagem "Em serviço" aparecerá no ecrã. Sem cartão de supervisor: Se o ecrã do TPA exibir a mensagem "Out of service", prima a tecla de seta para baixo para "Supervisor" e confirme com a tecla verde "Ok". Depois prima a tecla de seta para cima para "Ativar" e confirme com a tecla "Ok".

title: TPA fora de serviço: como reativar o equipamento?
text:
Premir novamente a seta para cima e seleccionar " 0 - Não utilizar". Em seguida, premir a seta para baixo e seleccionar "1 - NIB" ou "2- IBAN" e confirmar com "Ok". Introduzir o NIB ou IBAN e validar com "Ok". Um recibo de activação será então emitido e a mensagem "Em serviço" aparecerá no ecrã. - Ingenico: Seleccionar o menu "Supervisor" e premir "Activate TPA".

É a loja de aplicações do nosso Get Smart. Uma nova funcionalidade para melhorar o desempenho dos terminais dos nossos clientes que utilizam apps de terceiros nos nossos TPA.

Neste artigo, vamos te mostrar dicas práticas para proteger seu negócio contra fraudes, tanto nas vendas presenciais quanto no e-commerce, garantindo uma experiência segura para você e seus clientes.
Por que a segurança é tão importante?
Além de evitar prejuízos financeiros, investir em segurança ajuda a construir uma relação de confiança com o consumidor. “A segurança é um pilar essencial para fidelizar o cliente e garantir uma boa experiência de compra”, afirma Lourdes Quintana, superintendente de prevenção a atos ilícitos da Getnet Brasil.

Dicas de segurança para lojas físicas

title: Como vender com segurança no físico e no online - Getnet
text:
Confirme o Pix antes de liberar o produto
Não confie apenas no comprovante apresentado pelo cliente. Verifique no extrato ou no app do banco se o valor realmente caiu na conta.
Fique atento à troca de maquininhas
Golpistas podem tentar trocar sua maquininha por outra, desviando os pagamentos. Mantenha o equipamento sempre sob supervisão.
Cuidado com visitas técnicas inesperadas
Oriente sua equipe a não entregar equipamentos para supostos técnicos sem agendamento ou identificação oficial da empresa.
Dicas de segurança para o e-commerce
Monitore comportamentos suspeitos
Fique de olho em compras com muitos cartões diferentes ou pedidos em grande volume para o mesmo endereço.

Use plataformas seguras e invista em certificados SSL para garantir a proteção das informações de pagamento.
Evite prejuízos com chargeback
Antes de enviar o produto, confirme se o comprador é o titular do cartão. Guarde comprovantes e descreva bem os itens na fatura.

title: Como consultar CNPJ: confira passo a passo - Getnet
text:
Neste post, vamos te mostrar como consultar um CNPJ de forma simples e segura, direto no site oficial da Receita Federal. Bora conferir?
O que é o CNPJ e por que ele é importante?
O CNPJ é como o CPF das empresas. Ele identifica legalmente uma pessoa jurídica e reúne informações importantes, como:
Razão social e nome fantasia
Endereço
Atividade econômica (CNAE)
Situação cadastral (ativa, inativa, baixada etc.)
Dados dos sócios e administradores (QSA)
Consultar o CNPJ é útil para:
Verificar se uma empresa está regularizada
Confirmar dados antes de fechar uma compra ou parceria
Emitir notas fiscais corretamente
Validar fornecedores ou clientes

Como consultar um CNPJ no site da Receita Federal
Você pode fazer a consulta gratuitamente, sem precisar de login ou cadastro. Veja o passo a passo:
Passo 1: Acesse o site oficial da Receita Federal
Entre no link direto da consulta:
Acesse aqui
Passo 2: Digite o número do CNPJ
Insira o número completo do CNPJ (com 14 dígitos, apenas números) no campo indicado.
Passo 3: Marque o captcha e clique em “Consultar”
Confirme que você não é um robô e clique no botão para visualizar as informações.

title: Como consultar CNPJ: confira passo a passo - Getnet
text:
Passo 4: Veja os dados da empresa
Você terá acesso ao Comprovante de Inscrição e de Situação Cadastral, com todas as informações públicas da empresa.
O que significa a situação cadastral do CNPJ?
Ao consultar o CNPJ, você verá um campo chamado “Situação Cadastral”. Veja o que cada status significa:
Ativa: a empresa está regular e pode operar normalmente.
Inapta: a empresa deixou de entregar declarações obrigatórias.
Suspensa: pode haver pendências cadastrais ou fiscais.
Baixada: a empresa foi encerrada oficialmente.
Se você for fechar negócio com uma empresa, o ideal é que ela esteja com o CNPJ ativo.

Se você está pensando em empreender, mas ainda não sabe por onde começar, saiba que existem diversas ideias de pequenos negócios que podem ser altamente lucrativas. Com criatividade, planejamento e as ferramentas certas, é possível transformar uma paixão ou habilidade em uma fonte de renda estável. Neste artigo, listamos 9 ideias de negócios que exigem baixo investimento inicial e têm grande potencial de retorno.

title: Quer Empreender? Veja 9 ideias de negócios lucrativos - Getnet
text:
1. Alimentação por encomenda
Comidas caseiras, marmitas fitness, doces e bolos personalizados estão em alta. Se você gosta de cozinhar, pode começar vendendo para amigos e familiares e expandir com o tempo.
2. Brechó online
A revenda de roupas usadas em bom estado é uma tendência sustentável e lucrativa. Plataformas como Instagram e marketplaces facilitam a divulgação e venda.
3. Serviços de beleza em domicílio
Manicure, maquiagem, design de sobrancelhas e outros serviços de estética podem ser oferecidos em casa ou na casa do cliente, com baixo custo inicial.
4. Artesanato e produtos personalizados
Velas aromáticas, sabonetes artesanais, itens de decoração e presentes personalizados têm grande apelo e podem ser vendidos online ou em feiras locais.

5. Aulas particulares ou consultorias
Se você domina um assunto, pode oferecer aulas online ou presenciais, como reforço escolar, idiomas, música ou consultorias em áreas específicas.
6. Assistência técnica de eletrônicos
Consertos de celulares, notebooks e eletrodomésticos são sempre procurados. Com conhecimento técnico, é possível montar um negócio com boa demanda.
7. Pet sitter ou passeador de cães
O mercado pet está em crescimento. Se você gosta de animais, pode oferecer serviços de cuidado e passeio com pets na sua região.
8. Produção de conteúdo digital
Criar conteúdo para redes sociais, blogs ou canais no YouTube pode gerar renda com publicidade, parcerias e venda de produtos digitais.

Montar uma loja online com produtos específicos, como itens geek, produtos naturais ou acessórios para pets, pode atrair um público fiel e engajado.
